nodes.name: Ni foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: Ni foam was sonicated in 1M HCl solution for 10 min to remove the NiOx layer on the surface, and rinsed subsequently with deionized (DI) water and ethanol, then dried in air.
nodes.source_text: Ni foam was sonicated in 1M HCl solution for 10 min to remove the NiOx layer...

nodes.name: NiFe-OA chemical bath deposition
nodes.procedure: 2 mmol FeSO₄·7H₂O and 8 mmol NiSO₄·6H₂O were dissolved in 25 mL deionized water to form solution A (Ni/Fe = 4:1 molar ratio). Stoichiometric H₂C₂O₄·2H₂O (10 mmol) was dissolved in 25 mL deionized water or water/ethanol (3:1 v/v). pH of solution B adjusted to ~5 using 25% ammonia solution. Clean Ni foam (1.5×5 cm²) immersed vertically in solution B, preheated 5 min to form Ni-OA seed layer (Ni + H₂C₂O₄·2H₂O → NiC₂O₄·2H₂O + H₂). Solution A rapidly poured into solution B at 60°C. Stirred 30 min to grow NiFe-OA (Fe³⁺ + Ni²⁺ + C₂O₄·2H₂O²⁻ → NiFe-C₂O₄·2H₂O). Ni foam removed, rinsed 3× with DI water/ethanol, vacuum dried at 60°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Electrochemical topotactic transition
nodes.procedure: NiFe-OA/Ni foam used as working electrode in standard 3-electrode cell (graphite rod counter, Hg/HgO reference) with 1 M KOH electrolyte. Cyclic voltammetry: 0.9-1.7 V vs RHE, 30 cycles, 50 mV/s scan rate. Product: black NiFeOOH-T electrode (γ-Ni₀.₈Fe₀.₂OOH ultrathin nanosheets).
nodes.source_text: The topologic transition was carried out on the NiFe-OA electrode by using the cyclic voltammetry (CV) treatment with a potential window from 0.9 to 1.7 V vs.RHE for 30 cycles...

nodes.name: NiFeOOH-H hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ni foam (1.5×5 cm²) + 30 mL aqueous solution [0.6 mmol Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (Ni:Fe ≈ 1.25:1), 0.48 mmol Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O, 4 mmol urea] sealed in Teflon-lined autoclave. Hydrothermal reaction at 120°C for 12 h. Cooled to RT, washed 3× DI water/ethanol, vacuum dried 60°C/12 h. Product: NiFeOOH-H electrode.

nodes.name: Pt/C and Ir/C electrode preparation
nodes.procedure: A total of 5 mg of Pt/C (or Ir/C) was dispersed in a mixed solution consisting of 500 μL DI water, 495 μL ethanol, and 30 μL 5 wt% Nafion solution. After ultrasonicating for 30 min, the obtained ink was drop casted onto a Ni foam. The final loading amount of Pt/C (or Ir/C) was 1 mg cm⁻².

nodes.name: NiMoO4 hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: A piece of Ni foam (1.5×5 cm²) together with a 30 mL water solution containing Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.04 M) and (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O (0.01 M) were sealed in a Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave, and then was transferred into a drying oven and heated at 150°C for 6 h. After cooling down to the room temperature, the NiMoO4 electrode was obtained by washing the sample with DI water and ethanol for three times and drying it in vacuum at 60°C for 12 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeOOH-T retains cuboid-like morphology with newly formed cracks and rough surface featuring border-enriched small grains; NiFe-OA shows smooth cuboid-like particles of hundreds of nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The resulting NiFeOOH-T sample remained a cuboid-like morphology but with many newly formed cracks (Fig. 1d)... The rough surface of the particles (Fig. 1e) is a typical feature of topologically derived materials with border-enriched small grains.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeOOH-T consists of tightly intertwined ultrathin nanosheets tens of nm lateral size, ~5 nm thick with 0.21 nm (105) lattice fringes and abundant grain boundaries.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image in Fig. 2c shows that the NiFeOOH-T is composed of ultrathin NSs with tens of nanometers in lateral size... A lattice fringe with spacing of 0.21 nm recorded in the NiFeOOH-T (Fig. 2d) is in accordance with the interplanar distance of the (105) facets of NiFeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeOOH-T shows layered structures ~5 nm thick and hexagonal array of metal atoms; confirms nanosheet thickness and atomic arrangement.
nodes.evidence_snippet: layered structures were clearly observed in the side-view of HAADF-STEM image in Fig. 2g, demonstrating a thickness of ∼5 nm of the NiFeOOH-T NSs... the metal atoms were arranged in a hexagonal array pattern.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, and O elements throughout NiFeOOH-T nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding EDS elemental mappings in Fig. 2j show the uniform distributions of Ni, Fe and O elements in the NiFeOOH-T nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-OA shows sharp peaks of NiC₂O₄·2H₂O (JCPDS 25-0582) and FeC₂O₄·2H₂O (JCPDS 22-0635); NiFeOOH-T lacks (00n) peaks indicating thin nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of the NiFe-OA sample in Fig. S2 show the sharp characteristic diffraction peaks assigned to NiC₂O₄·2H₂O (JCPDS 25-0582) and FeC₂O₄·2H₂O (JCPDS 22-0635).

nodes.characterization_summary: Quasi in situ Raman during CV treatment shows complete phase transformation: NiFe-OA oxalate peaks (223/275, 533/587, 915, 1453/1471 cm⁻¹) → α-M(OH)₂/CO₃-LDH → γ-NiFeOOH (A₁g Ni-O at 545→556 cm⁻¹, broad NiOO⁻ 800-1200 cm⁻¹).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Characteristic Raman active peaks at 223/275 cm⁻¹, 533/587 cm⁻¹, 915 cm⁻¹ and 1453/1471 cm⁻¹ (Fig. 1f) were observed for the pristine NiFe-OA... indicating a complete transition into γ-NiFeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeOOH-T/NiFeOOH-H: Ni²⁺ (855.6/873.1 eV Ni-O, 856.9/874.7 eV Ni-OH), Fe³⁺ (712.4/725.4 eV); NiFeOOH-T Fe 2p shifts -0.5 eV vs NiFeOOH-H indicating topotactic modulation of Fe electronic structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the binding energy of Fe 2p in the NiFeOOH-T showed a significant negative shift of 0.5 eV compared with that of NiFeOOH-H... the peaks at 712.4 and 725.4 eV could be assigned to Fe 2p₃/₂ and Fe 2p₁/₂, respectively, indicating that Fe was in the +3 oxidation state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge: NiFeOOH-T shifts higher energy than NiFeOOH-H; Fe K-edge: NiFeOOH-T shifts lower energy; Ni L-edge: higher B/A ratio (0.57 vs 0.36); Fe L-edge: higher B/A ratio (2.16 vs 1.99), indicating modulated electronic states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the Ni K-edge spectra in Fig. 3a, the NiFeOOH-T shows a slight shift to higher energy than the NiFeOOH-H... the K-edge XANES spectrum of NiFeOOH-T shifted to lower energy compared with the NiFeOOH-H in Fig. 3b.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeOOH-T: Fe-O CN=5.0 (vs 5.5 NiFeOOH-H) confirming undercoordinated Fe sites; Ni-O CN≈4.5; M-O 1.5 Å, M-M 2.7 Å, Fe-M/Ni-M ~3.10 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the average coordination number of the Fe-O (∼5.0) in Table S4 is apparently smaller than that of NiFeOOH-H (∼5.5)... the prominent coordination peaks at 1.5 Å were assigned to the first shell coordination of M-O and other prominent peaks at 2.7 Å were associated with higher shell contributions in M-M coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeOOH-T C_dl=0.98 mF/cm² (vs 0.66 mF/cm² NiFeOOH-H) from scan-rate dependent CVs (10-300 mV/s, 0.72-0.82 V vs RHE); NiFeOOH-T Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ redox shifts -70 mV vs NiFeOOH-H.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiFeOOH-T has a higher ECSA (0.98 mFcm⁻²) than that (0.66 mFcm⁻²) of NiFeOOH-H (Fig. S20). The 50% enhancement of ECSA might be attributed to the small lateral size of nanosheets with abundant boundaries in NiFeOOH-T.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeOOH-T Rct = 0.33 Ω (lower than NiFeOOH-H at 0.44 Ω) indicating superior charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Rct value of NiFeOOH-T (0.33 Ω) is much smaller than that of NiFeOOH-H (0.44 Ω), as displayed in Fig. 4c.

nodes.characterization_summary: No detectable Ni or Fe ions in electrolyte after 72 h stability test, confirming excellent stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: we also monitored the concentration of Ni and Fe ions in the electrolyte during the stability test from 0 to 72 h by using inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) technique, the absence of Ni and Fe indicates the good stability.
